0345| # Run a command under a portable watchdog. ``timeout`` from GNU coreutils is not

0347| # kills it when the bound elapses, and the caller returns as soon as the command
0348| # itself is done. The watcher holds no stream of the caller and exits by itself
0349| # once the command is gone; it is stopped before the function returns, so no
0350| # process is left behind. BOUNDED_STATUS is 124 when the watchdog had to kill
0351| # the command.
0352| bounded_run() {

0354|     shift
0355|     stamp=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/forgel-code-check.$$
0356|     out=$stamp.out
0357|     done_marker=$stamp.done
0358|     killed_marker=$stamp.killed
0359|     rm -f "$out" "$done_marker" "$killed_marker"
0360|     if ! : > "$out"; then
0361|         return 1
0362|     fi
0363|     BOUNDED_STATUS=0
0364|     BOUNDED_OUTPUT=
0365|     "$@" > "$out" 2>/dev/null < /dev/null &
0366|     child=$!
0367|     (
0368|         # The watcher keeps no stream of the caller: a descriptor it held open
0369|         # would outlive the command it guards.
0370|         exec >/dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null
0371|         sleeper=
0372|         trap 'kill "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0' TERM
0373|         seconds=0
0374|         while [ "$seconds" -lt "$limit" ]; do
0375|             sleep 1 &
0376|             sleeper=$!
0377|             wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
0378|             sleeper=
0379|             seconds=$((seconds + 1))
0380|             if [ -e "$done_marker" ] || ! kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; then
0381|                 exit 0
0382|             fi
0383|         done
0384|         : > "$killed_marker" 2>/dev/null || true
0385|         kill -TERM "$child" 2>/dev/null || true
0386|     ) &
0387|     watcher=$!
0388|     wait "$child" || BOUNDED_STATUS=$?
0389|     : > "$done_marker"
0390|     kill -TERM "$watcher" 2>/dev/null || true
0391|     wait "$watcher" 2>/dev/null || true
0392|     BOUNDED_OUTPUT=$(sed -n 'p' "$out") || BOUNDED_OUTPUT=
0393|     if [ -e "$killed_marker" ]; then
0394|         BOUNDED_STATUS=124
0395|     fi

0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:

0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, under a hard time limit, and checks that
0017| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces the
0018| # installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0019| #
0020| # Environment variables:
0021| #   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
0022| #   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)
0023| #   FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE          local checkout to install from, without network
0024| #   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.1.0)
0025| #   FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY      repository URL used with FORGEL_CODE_TAG
0026| #   FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON          Python 3 interpreter (default: python3 on PATH)
0027| #   FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE         shell profile to edit (default: chosen from the login shell)
0028| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH  set to leave the shell profile untouched
0029| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT the same opt-out under its older name
0030| #   FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT         seconds the fresh-shell check may take (default: 10)
0031| #
0032| # The script is POSIX ``sh`` and safe to pipe into: it never reads stdin.

0042| # block is indistinguishable from one the file always had. The installer

0044| # that line, with the separator newline, together with the block.

0556| # remains of the process group after the grace period, and the caller returns
0557| # as soon as the command itself is done. Nothing the function starts survives
0558| # it. CHECK_STATUS is 124 when the bound elapsed.

0561|     shift

0563|     CHECK_OUTPUT=

0566|     fi

0578|     # everything the shell forked. Where it is unavailable ``signal_run`` walks
0579|     # the process tree instead.

0593|             sleeper=$!
0594|             wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
0595|             sleeper=
0596|             elapsed=$((elapsed + 1))
0597|             if ! kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; then
0598|                 exit 0
0599|             fi
0600|         done

0602|         signal_run TERM "$child"
0603|         sleep "$VERIFY_GRACE" 2>/dev/null || true
0604|         signal_run KILL "$child"

0611|         # finish so nothing outlives the check.
0612|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0613|         CHECK_STATUS=124
0614|     else
0615|         kill -TERM "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0616|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0617|     fi

0553| # Run a command under a hard time bound. ``timeout`` from GNU coreutils is not
0554| # required and is not used: the command runs in the background, a watchdog
0555| # sends a graceful stop when the bound elapses and forcefully stops whatever
0556| # remains of the process group after the grace period, and the caller returns
0557| # as soon as the command itself is done. Nothing the function starts survives
0558| # it. CHECK_STATUS is 124 when the bound elapsed.
0559| bounded_run() {
0560|     limit=$1
0561|     shift
0562|     CHECK_STATUS=0
0563|     CHECK_OUTPUT=
0564|     if ! create_check_dir; then
0565|         return 1
0566|     fi
0567|     out=$CHECK_DIR/output
0568|     timed_out=$CHECK_DIR/timed-out
0569|     saved_umask=$(umask)
0570|     umask 077
0571|     if ! : > "$out"; then
0572|         umask "$saved_umask"
0573|         cleanup_check
0574|         return 1
0575|     fi
0576|     # Job control, wherever the shell provides it in a script, gives the
0577|     # checked command its own process group, so the forceful stop reaches
0578|     # everything the shell forked. Where it is unavailable ``signal_run`` walks
0579|     # the process tree instead.
0580|     set -m 2>/dev/null || true
0581|     "$@" > "$out" 2>/dev/null < /dev/null &
0582|     CHECK_CHILD=$!
0583|     set +m 2>/dev/null || true
0584|     umask "$saved_umask"

0587|         exec > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null
0588|         sleeper=
0589|         trap 'kill "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0' TERM
0590|         elapsed=0

0592|             sleep 1 &
0593|             sleeper=$!
0594|             wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
0595|             sleeper=
0596|             elapsed=$((elapsed + 1))
0597|             if ! kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; then
0598|                 exit 0
0599|             fi
0600|         done
0601|         : > "$timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
0602|         signal_run TERM "$child"
0603|         sleep "$VERIFY_GRACE" 2>/dev/null || true
0604|         signal_run KILL "$child"
0605|     ) &
0606|     CHECK_WATCHER=$!
0607|     wait "$child" || CHECK_STATUS=$?
0608|     CHECK_CHILD=
0609|     if [ -e "$timed_out" ]; then
0610|         # The watchdog still owns the graceful then the forceful stop; let it
0611|         # finish so nothing outlives the check.
0612|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0613|         CHECK_STATUS=124
0614|     else
0615|         kill -TERM "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0616|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0617|     fi
0618|     CHECK_WATCHER=
0619|     CHECK_OUTPUT=$(cat "$out") || CHECK_OUTPUT=
0620|     cleanup_check
0621|     return 0
0622| }
